rationale: Both reviews are well-grounded with specific file:line citations, but X spends most of its budget validating already-resolved PR-history items and flagging minor doc/test-coverage nits, missing the sharper ground-truth concerns (ipc.py duplicate-function cleanup, DP wave fault-isolation/topology risk, shutdown reentrancy). Y independently surfaces several high-severity, well-reasoned bugs (wave-wide failure from one bad request, silent cross-request output substitution, a dead code branch validated by a test of unreachable logic, shutdown-ordering races) and its ipc.py alias finding and shutdown-reentrancy note land close to the ground truth's _tensor_from_shm/premark concerns, giving it both better recall and more concrete, code-level remediation.
